summary: Derived places now get a human-readable name even without a Google geocode-cache hit (issue #10 option 1): the place label falls back to the most common Life360 address string among the fixes that built the place. Zero new API calls, zero billing exposure — Life360 already sends the address on every fix; the label is computed in memory from data the rollup already reads and written through the existing label column. Typed feature rather than fix because a place being unlabelled was not broken behaviour, it was the documented absence of a capability.
details: Label precedence is Google geocode cache first (canonical whenever the cache has a hit), Life360's address mode second — the deliberate relaxation of the 2026-08-19 Google-cache-only labelling decision
Each closed stay carries the mode of its own fixes' addresses (most frequent, first occurrence on a tie, none when no fix has an address), computed once at segmentation time
Fail-closed: no cache hit and no addressed fixes leaves the place unlabelled, never a guessed or empty label
A place that already has a label keeps it through cycles whose new fixes carry no address — absence of new evidence never wipes a written label
No geocode calls or network egress added; no schema change (the existing presence_derived_places label column is used as-is)
limitations: presence_stays stores no address column, so each labelling cycle sees the Life360 addresses of that cycle's new stays only; a place's label tracks the most recent evidence at the place rather than a lifetime mode of every fix that ever built it
a place that reclassifies between home and work (the Speed 2 recheck write) starts from the cache-only label again; its Life360 fallback label rebuilds on the next clustering cycle
